slides.title: Particle, emitter and particle system
slides.source: Source: Chapter 9, “A particle system is a birth–life–death loop”; glossary, Particles.
slides.notes: The arc uses gravity 260; the fountain fires 12 a second with a seeded speed and angle.
slides.picture: One particle follows an arc from birth to death. Then an emitter fires a stream, and the emitter plus its rules make a particle system.

new_texts: One small short-lived sprite or mesh in an effect.
A particle is a point with an age. It is born, moves by the rules, and dies at its lifetime.
all_texts: One small short-lived sprite or mesh in an effect.
A particle is a point with an age. It is born, moves by the rules, and dies at its lifetime.

new_texts: The emitter is the spawner. It fires new particles at a steady rate; each one lives and fades.
all_texts: One small short-lived sprite or mesh in an effect.
The emitter is the spawner. It fires new particles at a steady rate; each one lives and fades.

new_texts: The emitter plus the rules for its particles.
The emitter and the rules it spawns by are the particle system.

slides.title: Amount, lifetime and steady state
slides.source: Source: Chapter 9, “The timing model: one emission cycle”; glossary, Particles.
slides.notes: Live count is computed from the birth times: amount 60, lifetime 2 s, so 30 born a second.
slides.picture: A chart of live count over six seconds with amount 60 and lifetime 2 seconds: it climbs for two seconds then stays at 60.

slides.title: Gravity, damping and the age curves
slides.source: Source: Chapter 9, “Particle shaders”; Godot ParticleProcessMaterial reference, damping; glossary, Particles.
slides.notes: Gravity is added to velocity each 1/60 s step. Damping 150 takes a speed of 300 to 0 in 2 s. Damping is defined in the Godot class reference, not in the chapter.
slides.picture: Arcs with and without gravity; dots slowing under damping; circles shrinking along a scale curve; circles fading along a colour ramp.

new_texts: Constant downward acceleration applied to particles.
Each step adds gravity × step time to the velocity. The path bends into an arc.
all_texts: Constant downward acceleration applied to particles.
Each step adds gravity × step time to the velocity. The path bends into an arc.

new_texts: The rate at which particles lose velocity. 100 takes a speed of 100 to 0 in 1 second.
A DOT EVERY 0.1 S, START SPEED 300
stops after 2.0 s, 299 px from the start
speed after t seconds = 300 − 150 × t, never below 0
Damping subtracts speed each second until the particle stops.

slides.title: Before you trust a particle effect
slides.source: Source: Chapter 9, “Verify” and “What is still unverified”.
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

new_texts: Is the effect's parent still visible when it fires?
Is the texture set, and is disable_z on in 2D?
Do amount, lifetime and explosiveness give the count and timing I meant?
Does a one-shot restart on every later use?
Is the visibility rect big enough, and is overdraw cheap on a real GPU?
Did a person watch it on a screen, and does it read as one clear effect?
A headless test proves state. Only a screen shows the effect.
